content: ## Metadata_Start ## code: en ## title: Capacity Management ## slug: events-capacity-management ## seoTitle: Capacity Management ## description: ## contentType: Markdown ## Metadata_End With the Capacity Management v1 release, we added logic to include the pending registrations when calculating the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}}. Now, the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} is calculated by subtracting the completed and pending registrations from the {{variable.Object_Event}}’s {{variable.Field_ETEvent_TotalCapacity}}, which the Events Organizer sets in {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. Capacity is checked at multiple points during the registration process. If the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} reaches zero, the user will see a message and cannot continue until they remove the sold-out item from their cart. In addition, we enhanced batch processing to reconcile capacity counts by including new pending registration counts once every minute. While this is not a complete solution that addresses all use cases, it does address many of the most common situations that cause over-enrollment. ***Note:** This does not include waitlist capacities.* ## Important Prerequisites For Capacity Management to work correctly, you must perform the following. * Upgrade your org to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} {{variable.Product_Events}} version 4.23 or later. * Review all custom flows, as they may interfere with functionality. * Click the {{variable.Button_SchedBatchEventRegSubmi}} button to turn on batching. If the Batch Event Registration Submission scheduled job is already running, click the **Disable Batch Event Registration Submission Job** button and then click {{variable.Button_SchedBatchEventRegSubmi}} again to ensure that all jobs are rescheduled correctly. ![image-20240508-131739](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/image-20240508-131739.png){height="" width=""} ## High-Level Diagrams ### Single-Screen Experience ![Capacity Mgt - Initial Phase 1 - Simple \(single-screen\)](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Capacity%20Mgt%20-%20Initial%20Phase%201%20-%20Simple%20%28single-screen%29.png){height="" width=""} ### Multi-Screen Experience ![Capacity Mgt - Initial Phase 1 - Standard \(multi-screen\)](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Capacity%20Mgt%20-%20Initial%20Phase%201%20-%20Standard%20%28multi-screen%29.png){height="" width=""} ## Post-Enhancement (May 2024) State ### What’s New? #### Salesforce * Capacity calculations have been modified. The pending count value is now included in the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} field calculation, ensuring that queued pending registrations will be removed from the available capacity. This change allows us to determine the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} more accurately. * We have expanded the integration between the webapp and {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} so that the following will occur. * Potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s will see a more detailed error message when {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} is unavailable. * {{variable.Object_Event}}’s will now track pending registrations so they can be used in capacity calculations. * A batch job will reconcile pending and completed registration counts as the registrations are completed. #### Webapp The webapp will continue to make the same number of calls to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. Each time the webapp makes a call to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}, the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} will be checked for availability. * If a call returns no available capacity, the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} will see a message and cannot continue with their registration. * Single-Page layout: Two calls are made. 1. {{variable.CapMgmt_StartCheckoutCall}} occurs when the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} clicks the **Payment** or **Place Your Order** button. 2. {{variable.CapMgmt_FinalCheckoutCall}} rechecks the capacity if the {{variable.CapMgmt_StartCheckoutCall}} is successful. It then changes the {{variable.Object_EventRegistrationSub}} record {{variable.Field_ERS_Status}} to “Processing” if capacity is available. * Multi-Page layout: Three calls are made. 1. {{variable.CapMgmt_DraftCall}} occurs when the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} clicks the **Checkout** / **Continue** button after entering their information. 2. {{variable.CapMgmt_StartCheckoutCall}} occurs after the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} clicks the **Payment** or **Place Your Order** button. 3. {{variable.CapMgmt_FinalCheckoutCall}} rechecks the capacity if the {{variable.CapMgmt_StartCheckoutCall}} is successful. It then changes the {{variable.Object_ERS}} record {{variable.Field_ERS_Status}} to “Processing” if capacity is available. #### Updated Equations * {{variable.Object_Event}} Object * The {{variable.Field_Event_CapacitThreshLimit}} now includes {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s with an {{variable.Object_EventRegistrationSub}} {{variable.Field_ERS_Status}} = “Draft,” ensuring the number of remaining Tickets ({{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}}) is correct. * The {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} formula now includes the new {{variable.Field_Event_PendingCapacity}} (conference360__Pending_Capacity__c) field in its calculation. * {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} = {{variable.Field_ETEvent_TotalCapacity}} - {{variable.Field_Event_AttendeLimitBuffer}} - {{variable.Field_ETEvent_Registered}} - {{variable.Field_Event_PendingCapacity}} * {{variable.Object_Session}} Object * {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s will now see an accurate number of remaining {{variable.Object_Session}} spots when registering for an {{variable.Object_Event}}. * The {{variable.Field_Session_QuantityRemainin}} formula now includes the new {{variable.Field_Session_PendingCapacity}} (conference360__Pending_Capacity__c) field in its calculation. * {{variable.Field_Session_QuantityRemainin}} = {{variable.Field_Session_QuantityAvailabl}} - ({{variable.Field_Session_Registered}} + {{variable.Field_Session_PendingCapacity}}) * {{variable.Object_EventItem}} Object * {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s will now see an accurate number of remaining {{variable.Object_EventItem}}s when registering for an {{variable.Object_Event}}. * The {{variable.Object_EventItem}}'s {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantiRemain}} formula now includes the new {{variable.Field_EVItem_PendingCapacity}} (conference360__Pending_Capacity__c) field in its calculation to improve the accuracy of the {{variable.Object_EventItem}}’s available capacity. * {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantiRemain}} = {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantityAvai}} - ({{variable.Field_EVItem_Registered}} + {{variable.Field_EVItem_PendingCapacity}}). ### Detailed Breakdown of the Registration Journey 1. The {{variable.CapMgmt_DraftCall}} to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} includes a capacity validation and prevents a registration if the {{variable.Object_Event}} is sold out. (Multi-Page layout only) 1. {{variable.CapMgmt_Webapp}} The potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} browses the {{variable.Object_Event}}’ webpage, goes to the registration page, and enters their registration information. (This step is before they submit their payment information.) 2. {{variable.CapMgmt_Webapp}} A {{variable.CapMgmt_DraftCall}} is made to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. In the {{variable.CapMgmt_DraftCall}}, the registration request is not submitted. This allows the following to occur: 1) Create a draft {{variable.Object_ERS}} record in {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}, and 2) check capacity. 3. {{variable.CapMgmt_Salesforce}} * {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} creates an {{variable.Object_ERS}} record with {{variable.Field_ERS_Status}} = “Draft.” * {{variable.CapMgmt_New}} The validation includes {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s with {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_RegistrStatus}} = “Processing“ (i.e., registrations currently pending in the queue while they are being processed) in the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}} field calculation. If no capacity is left, {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} returns a {{variable.CapMgmt_Failure}} status with a message to the webapp. 4. {{variable.CapMgmt_Webapp}} * {{variable.CapMgmt_New}} If the call to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} returns a {{variable.CapMgmt_Failure}} status (i.e., the {{variable.Object_Event}}’ is sold out), the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} will see an error message and be prevented from proceeding. 2. Checkout Process Start * For the Single-Page layout, the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} enters their information. * If the {{variable.Object_Event}}’ is a paid {{variable.Object_Event}}’, the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} enters a payment method and associated payment information. 3. Checkout Process Completion (The user clicks the **Payment** or **Place Your Order** button.) 1. {{variable.CapMgmt_Webapp}} A {{variable.CapMgmt_StartCheckoutCall}} is made to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} to check capacity. * If this is a Single-Page layout, it also creates a draft {{variable.Object_ERS}} record in {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} since this is the first time {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} has been called. 2. {{variable.CapMgmt_Salesforce}} * {{variable.CapMgmt_New}} Capacity validation occurs. * The new capacity calculation logic, which includes {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s with {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_RegistrStatus}} = “Pending,” is used. * If no capacity is left, {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} returns a {{variable.CapMgmt_Failure}} status with a message to the webapp. * If this is a Single-Page layout (i.e., the first call to the webapp), {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} creates an {{variable.Object_ERS}} record with {{variable.Field_ERS_Status}} = “Draft.” 3. {{variable.CapMgmt_Webapp}} * {{variable.CapMgmt_New}} If the call to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} returns a {{variable.CapMgmt_Failure}} status (i.e., the {{variable.Object_Event}}’ is sold out), {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} displays an error message, and the webapp prevents the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} from proceeding. 4. {{variable.CapMgmt_Webapp}} If the {{variable.CapMgmt_StartCheckoutCall}} is successful because capacity is available, the webapp will make a {{variable.CapMgmt_FinalCheckoutCall}} to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. In this call, the webapp submits the registration request, which causes several registration-related things to happen in {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}. 5. {{variable.CapMgmt_Salesforce}} Processes the call from the webapp. * {{variable.CapMgmt_New}} The capacity is validated. * The new capacity calculation logic, which includes {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s with {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_RegistrStatus}} = “Pending,” is used. * If no capacity is left, {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} returns a {{variable.CapMgmt_Failure}} status with a message to the webapp. * If the {{variable.Object_Event}}’ has {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RemainingCapacit}}, {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} will update the draft {{variable.Object_ERS}} record from the previous step to {{variable.Field_ERS_Status}} = “To Process.” * {{variable.CapMgmt_New}} The pending count value will include the registrations that are in the queue to be processed. 6. {{variable.CapMgmt_Webapp}} {{variable.CapMgmt_Enhanced}} If the call to {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} returns an error, the potential {{variable.Object_Attendee}} will see an error message about no availability. 4. The batch process, which runs once every minute and is processed on a first-in-first-out basis, will process the registrations and reconcile the pending count field. 1. {{variable.Object_Invoice}}s and {{variable.Object_LineItem}}s will be created. 2. {{variable.Object_Attendee}} records will be created. 3. The {{variable.Object_ERS}} record will be updated to {{variable.Field_ERS_Status}} = “Complete.” 4. {{variable.CapMgmt_New}} The pending count will be updated to remove the processed registrations. 5. All other processing actions, including capturing financial transaction information and roll-up calculations, will be completed. 6. A cache invalidation request will be sent.
